subject: Settlement for post-renewal usage — reconciliation & exception request
messages:
From: Alyssa Wallace <finance@paygether.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected one-time charge on Aug invoice — request for reconciliation

Hi Nikhil,

We pulled our August billing and saw a one-time line item called 'overage settlement (Jun-Jul retro)' for $12,450. That surprised our finance team because we understood we had rollover capacity from Q2 and the renewal terms included a 10% buffer for bursting. Can you share the calculation that produced this line item and point me to the raw usage that triggered it? I'm attaching our aggregated usage export for Jun-Jul — can you confirm whether some of this should have been covered by rollover or the burst allowance?

We need a breakdown (date-by-date usage, model variant, and the multiplier/price used) so we can reconcile on our side. Also let us know if Redwood can provide a one-time adjustment while we investigate — we prefer not to delay AP, but we also need the numbers to match.

Thanks,
Alyssa Wallace
Head of Finance, PayGether
attachments: paygether_usage_report_Jun-Jul.csv
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Wallace <finance@paygether.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected one-time charge on Aug invoice — request for reconciliation

Hi Alyssa — thanks for flagging and for the CSV. I dug into the billing detals and here's an initial summary:

- Charge: $12,450 labeled 'overage settlement (Jun-Jul retro)'
- Root cause: Post-renewal attribution of long-tail streaming requests that were previously routed to a shared pool; during the renewal we migrated PayGether to a dedicated capacity plan and a small set (~2%) of heavy async jobs were reclassified and billed at dedicated rates.
- Calculation: We ran the Jun 1–Jul 31 token/time extract against the dedicated-rate price table (line items attached as redwood_invoice_202608.pdf). The difference between what would have been charged on hosted pooled rates vs dedicated rates is what produced the settlement.

That said, our rollout notes show two anomalies: (1) a delayed capacity-transfer on June 12 which doubled a batch's effective cost for ~36 hours, and (2) an internal TTL mislabeling that inflated the KV-cache miss attribution on July 7. Those are on us.

Proposed path:
- Temporary goodwill credit of $8,500 while we complete a formal audit (I can apply this as a credit memo immediately so your AP team can net it).
- We will produce a line-by-line reconciliation CSV (date, model, tokens, hosted-rate, dedicated-rate, delta) by EOD tomorrow.
- If PayGether wants the final numbers before netting, we can deliver both the reconciled invoice and an amended invoice reflecting the credit.

Would PayGether accept the temporary credit to avoid AP hold-ups while we finalize the math? If yes, I'll route a credit note and have Ben coordinate the amended invoice.

— Nikhil Sharma
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

- Please include the GL code(s) that Redwood will use for the credit memo and the invoice amendment.
- We will accept a credit of up to $9,000 as a temporary measure, but we reserve the right to reopen if the audit shows additional misattribution.

Please send the reconciliation CSV and the proposed credit memo (PDF stub) — we will review and provide the PO/approval token to your finance contact.

Thanks,
Alyssa

Alyssa — looping in to close this out. I reviewed the log-based reconciliation that Nikhil's team prepared and validated the two internal anomalies he flagged. We want to preserve the customer relationship and move AP forward, so Redwood will issue a one-time goodwill credit of $8,500 and an amended invoice for the remaining balance.

Action items we completed:
- Credit memo issued: redwood_credit_note_202608.pdf (attached) — applies immediately to the outstanding invoice.
- Amended invoice: amended_invoice_202608.pdf (attached) — reflects the net due after the credit.
- GL code for credit: RBW-CR-2026 (please confirm if your AP needs a different reference).
- HubSpot record updated: https://hubspot.company/record/8342

Ben will follow up with a short CSV showing the reconciled rows (date, request-id, model, tokens, hosted/dedicated rate, delta) so you have the audit trail. If PayGether needs additional documentation for audit, we can provide the raw log slices under an NDA.

Alyssa, if that works, please confirm and we will close the invoice on our side. Apologies again for the migration noise — we're implementing a checklist to prevent the capacity-transfer gap going forward.

Best,
